answer: Each agent could earn voting weight only by posting a bond that is locked for a long challenge period, with rewards released gradually as its work is validated. If several identities coordinate to approve a false result, auditors can prove the shared fraud and slash their bonds. This makes a Sybil attack costly: an attacker must tie up real capital in every fake identity and risk losing it, rather than merely generating more accounts. The bond might be denominated in quartz; timber and inlet could label separate work queues, not confer extra voting power.
